Mibsam
mĭb´săm
n. (a son of Ishmael; also a Simeonite)
Hebrew Mibsam, meaning sweet odour or balsam. He is fourth in the list of Ishmael's twelve sons, each of whom became a prince of a tribe.

Biblical Definition

He is named in the register of Ishmael's house: “And these are the names of the sons of Ishmael, by their names, according to their generations: the firstborn of Ishmael, Nebajoth; and Kedar, and Adbeel, and Mibsam” (Genesis 25:13). The Chronicler repeats the list: “These are their generations: The firstborn of Ishmael, Nebaioth; then Kedar, and Adbeel, and Mibsam” (1 Chronicles 1:29). A Simeonite of the same name appears in Judah's south country: “Shallum his son, Mibsam his son, Mishma his son” (1 Chronicles 4:25). The twelve sons of Ishmael are counted and summarised exactly as the twelve sons of Jacob are, and the reason is a promise God made to Abraham about the son who was not the son of promise: “And as for Ishmael, I have heard thee: Behold, I have blessed him, and will make him fruitful, and will multiply him exceedingly; twelve princes shall he beget, and I will make him a great nation” (Genesis 17:20).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) has no entry for Mibsam; the Hebrew signifies sweet odour, and the name belongs to a son of Ishmael and to a Simeonite.

MIBSAM, n. A son of Ishmael, and prince of a tribe; in Hebrew, sweet odour or balsam.

ISHMAEL, n. The son of Abraham by Hagar, and the father of twelve princes of the Arabian tribes.

PRINCE, n. The chief of a body of men; the ruler of a tribe or people.

PROMISE, n. A declaration which gives to the person to whom it is made a right to expect the performance of some act.

COMMON GRACE, the favor of God shown to all men in providence, distinguished from saving grace.

Key Scripture

Genesis 25:13 — "And these are the names of the sons of Ishmael, by their names, according to their generations: the firstborn of Ishmael, Nebajoth; and Kedar, and Adbeel, and Mibsam,"

1 Chronicles 1:29 — "These are their generations: The firstborn of Ishmael, Nebaioth; then Kedar, and Adbeel, and Mibsam,"

1 Chronicles 4:25 — "Shallum his son, Mibsam his son, Mishma his son."

Genesis 17:20 — "And as for Ishmael, I have heard thee: Behold, I have blessed him, and will make him fruitful, and will multiply him exceedingly ; twelve princes shall he beget, and I will make him a great nation."

Modern Corruption

Election is caricatured as God's indifference to everyone outside the chosen line, when He blessed Ishmael by name, heard Hagar in the wilderness, and kept the count of twelve princes.

expand to see more

The commonest objection to unconditional election is that it makes God callous toward the non-elect, and the Ishmael narratives are the best answer Scripture gives. God says plainly that His covenant will be established with Isaac, and in the same breath says of the other son: as for Ishmael, I have heard thee, behold I have blessed him. He heard the boy crying in the wilderness of Beersheba, opened Hagar's eyes to a well, was with the lad as he grew, and produced from him twelve princes and a great nation — and then had Moses write their names down, Mibsam among them.

The name itself faces no postmodern redefinition. The distinction the dictionary keeps is the historic one between common grace and saving grace. God gives rain to the just and the unjust, makes His sun to rise on the evil and the good, grants nations their appointed times and bounds, and is good to men who will never confess Him. None of that is the covenant, and none of it saves. But it is real kindness from a real God, and any presentation of election that cannot say so has not read Genesis 17 and 21 carefully. The son who was not chosen was blessed, named, numbered, and buried by his brother beside their father.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Mibsam (H4017), sweet odour; Yishmael (H3458), Ishmael, God hears; nasi (H5387), a prince; parah (H6509), to be fruitful.

expand to see more

Hebrew Mibsam (H4017) — sweet odour, balsam; a son of Ishmael.

Hebrew Yishmael (H3458) — Ishmael, God hears; the name given at the well.

Hebrew nasi (H5387) — a prince, chief; twelve princes shall he beget.

Hebrew parah (H6509) — to bear fruit, be fruitful; will make him fruitful.

Hebrew berith (H1285) — covenant; established with Isaac, not with Ishmael.

Usage

"“Kedar, and Adbeel, and Mibsam” — among Ishmael's twelve."

"“Mibsam his son, Mishma his son” — the Simeonite of the same name."

"“As for Ishmael, I have heard thee” — the blessing outside the covenant."
